newsitem.title: RUSSIA: All hostages in Tajikistan alive - TASS.
newsitem.headline: All hostages in Tajikistan alive - TASS.

text.p: All 14 hostages, including U.N. observers and journalists, held by Tajik rebels are alive, Itar-Tass news agency quoted Russia's Deputy Prime Minister Vitaly Ignatenko as saying on Friday.

Ignatenko has been talking to the rebels by telephone. A leader of the Islamic rebel group, Bakhram Sadirov, told the U.N. mission in the Tajik capital Dushanbe earlier that his troops had shot a U.N. military observer dead.

Bakhram Sadirov and his brother Rizvon are holding three U.N. observers -- two Swiss and a Ukrainian -- along with four Russian journalists, four staff of the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR and the Tajik security minister who was seized when he arrived to negotiate.

Earlier on Friday the hostage takers had threatened to take their captives to the mountains and launch a guerrilla war against the government if their demand -- a swap of the hostages for a group of their supporters -- was not met.
The Tajik government had flown 35 supporters of the hostage-takers into Tajikistan from Afghanistan on Thursday.

In a separate report Tass said a helicopter carrying 25 Sadirovs' fighters had just landed at their base. The report appeared to indicate the swap was under way, but no further details were immediately availiable.
